thread:
dev-support: Heads up — a customer reported our go SDK is breaking their CI after they upgraded to Go 1.21. They see a checksum mismatch when `go get` hits a tagged release we vendor. Repro attached.

alex: ugh. do we still have any `replace` directives that point at forks/pseudo-versions?

maria: I think we added a temporary replace in the last release to work around a third-party tagging issue. It might be leaking into published module metadata.

dev-support: Here's the minimal repro they sent (from their CI):
```bash
# in their repo
GO111MODULE=on GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v1.4.2
# error
verifying github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v1.4.2: checksum mismatch
        downloaded: h1:abc...
        go.sum:    h1:def...
```

maria: Asking them to `go env -w GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct` didn't help?

dev-support: They said it fails in our CI and their local `go list -m all` shows our module replaced: `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk => ../local/go-sdk` (they have a local replace for internal testing). When they remove the replace, `go get` succeeds locally but CI still fails.

alex: CI still failing implies the published module zip (or go.mod) references a pseudo-version or a replaced path that the proxy resolves differently. Can you paste our published go.mod for v1.4.2?

eng-ml: grabbing it from the release tag...

eng-ml: Published go.mod from tag v1.4.2:
```
module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk

require (
    github.com/some/dependency v0.9.0
)

replace github.com/thirdparty/dep => github.com/thirdparty/dep v0.0.0-20231201120000-abcdef123456
```

maria: there it is — the `replace` with a pseudo-version got committed into the tag. When the proxy fetches the zip, `go.sum` in the downstream may not match if the module graph resolved differently. We shouldn't publish tags with `replace` directives that point directly to pseudo-versions.

dev-support: Customer says they can't change their CI (enterprise constraints). They want a fix from us.

alex: Action plan: (1) publish a patch tag v1.4.3 that removes the replace (or replaces it with a proper versioned module path), (2) ask customers to `go clean -modcache` if still blocked, (3) add CI check to fail releases that include non-local `replace` directives.

maria: I'll prepare v1.4.3 PR that replaces `replace ... => ... vX.Y.Z` with the proper versioned dependency. Should we also add a RELEASE_NOTES entry explaining checksum mismatch fallout?

dev-support: yes, include notes and a short mitigation they can apply: run `go env -w GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct` and `go clean -modcache` on CI runners. But emphasize we will ship a fixed tag.

ci-bot: Build 12458 triggered for branch fix/go-mod-remove-replace — tests: unit=✓ integ=✓ publish-check=failed (detected replace directive in go.mod).

alex: publish-check failure is expected. patch branch looks good. Two questions: will cutting v1.4.3 change the module checksum consumers get? It will, but checksums should align since the published tag will have normalized go.mod without pseudo-version `replace`.

maria: Also adding a release-time linter to our release workflow: disallow `replace` directives unless they point to `../` local paths and block tag creation if found. I'll open a PR in infra.

dev-support: Customer replied: they tried `go clean -modcache` and reran CI; still failing intermittently. They have a private proxy that cached the old zip. We should publish the patch and ask them to purge their proxy cache.

alex: note for ops: when we publish v1.4.3, update the release artifact in our internal docs and ping partner integrators to purge caches (Artifactory/goproxy).

eng-ml: follow-up: I checked our release script — we `git tag` from the workspace without a fresh clone, so local `replace` can slip in. I'll update the script to `git archive` the tree at the commit and build from that clean tree before tagging.

maria: PRs opened: #402 (remove replace + update deps), #403 (release linter), #404 (release script hygiene).

dev-support: I'll coordinate with the customer and update the support ticket: provisional workaround + ETA for v1.4.3. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

alex: quick note for the knowledgebase — write an article: "Why go.mod replace directives can break downstream consumers" with examples + steps (remove replace, publish tag, purge proxy).

maria: creating KB draft now. will ping for review.

dev-support: closing loop once customer confirms CI green on their side.
